data.narrative:
Intuitive Machines is a publicly traded Space & Aerospace company founded by Steve Altemus, Kam Ghaffarian, and Tim Crain, having raised $305M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of five same-sector, same-stage comparables: SpaceX ($1.6T), Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B), and Astroscale ($840M).

The peer-median method is applicable and yields a direct valuation anchor. The median valuation across the five-company peer set is $7.6B, with a wide range from $840M at the low end (Astroscale) to $1.6T at the high end (SpaceX). This dispersion reflects meaningful differences in mission scope, revenue scale, and market position within the space sector. A revenue-based multiple approach using the public Space & Aerospace P/S median of 24.6x could theoretically apply, but cannot be executed here owing to the absence of Intuitive Machines' revenue data on file.

The triangulation produces a valuation range of $6.4B to $8.7B, centered on $7.6B. This median reflects the peer-comparable method alone, as only one method was executable. Key uncertainties include the true revenue and profitability trajectory relative to peers, the company's positioning within lunar and cislunar markets, and the applicability of SpaceX and Rocket Lab as meaningful anchors given their substantially larger scale. The wide peer range ($840M to $1.6T) underscores sector heterogeneity and limits narrow precision.
